sources.entry: AI Dev Toolkit - 196 production-ready frameworks for AI engineering: multi-agent orchestration, MCP server configs, vibe coding workflows, RAG pipelines, and agentic deployment guides. 97 free samples available.

summary.one_liner: A free collection of copy-paste AI prompts and sample workflows for developers (code review, security, debugging, testing, MCP servers, vibe coding), with a paid toolkit upsell.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents a set of free sample prompts organized into categories such as vibe coding, AI agents, code review, security, context engineering, MCP tools, meta-prompting, architecture, debugging, testing, and database/SQL. Each sample is listed in a table with a one-line description, for example a Cursor rules generator, a senior-style PR reviewer, a SQL query optimizer, and an MCP server builder. The README says the prompts are meant to be copied into an LLM such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or Codex, with the user supplying their own codebase context. It also describes a quick-start example of pasting a code review prompt and a diff. A paid "Full Toolkit" is promoted with more resources, but the README does not show the contents of those resources. Contributions are accepted via pull requests, and the README refers to a CONTRIBUTING.md file.
use_cases: Generate a .cursorrules file for a project
Review a pull request with an LLM prompt
Audit code for security vulnerabilities with a prompt
Write unit tests with an AI prompt
Optimize slow SQL queries with an LLM
Build an MCP server with an AI assistant
Root-cause a bug using a structured prompt
how_to_run: Pick a prompt from the categories listed in the README
Paste it into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or another LLM
Provide your codebase context when the prompt asks for it
notable: Only 168 free samples are included; the README points to a paid toolkit for the remaining resources
Prompts are organized into 12 categories with a short table for each
Written to be pasted into any LLM, with no code to install
Lists a free-vs-paid comparison that promotes a $9 one-time Full Toolkit
Written and maintained by an autonomous AI agent, per the README
caveats: Most of the advertised 266 resources are in the paid toolkit, not this repo
Samples are plain prompt text, so results depend on the LLM and the context the user provides
The README has no install steps, tests, or versioning details
